text: ratings simulated truth known: 120 teams 4 12 members rate team’s climate support receive. Teams two types, supportive strained, differ average ratings , climate, much teams type vary. model never sees type; kept check classification later.

title: Class enumeration in mixture models

text: bootstrap likelihood ratio test (McLachlan, 1987) compares two candidates differ one class. Data sets simulated smaller candidate candidates re-estimated . title: Covariates, outcomes and staged estimation
text: estimate mean external variable profile, call three_step() data data frame outcome variable. default method, BCH, corrects classification error; standard errors clustered groups. compare profiles, call three_step() contrast = "pairs", returns difference profile means Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value. Maximum likelihood correction. method = "ml", assigned profile becomes indicator true profile whose classification errors fixed measurement model, external variable normal within profile, variance. table adds variance. variable close normal within profiles, ML gives smaller standard errors BCH; skewed, BCH robust choice. see effect ignoring classification error, call three_step() method = "modal", treats case’s probable profile known.

Attendance rises 0.036 per unit previous grade within profile (95% interval 0.001 0.071), forum posting 0.004 (interval -0.037 0.045). effects small profile differences, BIC lower without (16986.9 16992.1), profiles owe separation previous grades.

code: get_results(fit, "classification_errors", level = "groups")  # group-level errors get_results(fit, "bch_weights", level = "individuals")       # BCH weights per case three_step(fit, data = course_engagement, outcome = "previous_grade",            method = "proportional")        # weighting by posterior probabilities three_step(fit, data = course_engagement, outcome = "previous_grade",            method = "ml", variance = "equal")  # ML with one shared variance three_step(fit, data = course_engagement, outcome = "previous_grade",            vcov_type = "independent")      # standard errors without clustering r3step(fit, data = course_engagement, covariates = "previous_grade",        vcov_type = "observed")             # observed-information standard errors measurement <- multilpa(course_engagement,                         vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read",                                  "forum_post", "attendance"),                         id = "student", n_profiles = 2,                         n_group_classes = 1, seed = 1)  # a one-class measurement fit fit_staged(course_engagement,            vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post",                     "attendance"),            id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,            measurement = measurement)      # stage two from that fit multilpa(course_engagement,          vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post",                   "attendance"),          id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,          start = starting_values(fit, what = "measurement"),          fixed = "variances")              # hold chosen parameters fixed parameter_inference(staged)                # standard errors of the estimated stage

title: Evaluating a multilevel latent profile model
text: course_engagement one row per course enrolment: 1,422 enrolments 106 students. student identifies group, five activity measures (browse, lectures, forum_read, forum_post, attendance) indicators, standardized within course.
code: library(latents)

title: Evaluating a multilevel latent profile model
text: fit model, call multilpa() vars indicators, id group, n_profiles number profiles, n_group_classes number group classes, n_starts number random EM starts, seed reproducible starts.
code: fit <- multilpa(course_engagement,                 vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post",                          "attendance"),                 id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,                 n_starts = 3, seed = 1)

title: Evaluating a multilevel latent profile model

title: Evaluating a multilevel latent profile model
text: Information criteria compare candidates fitted, possible models. Classification measures describe fitted model; misspecified model can still classify sharply. Wald intervals assume converged fit variance bound, conditional chosen numbers profiles classes. Unmodelled dependence indicators can make extra classes look better.

title: Growth mixture models: classes of trajectories
text: Latent class growth analysis (Nagin 2005) gives every class trajectory. Everyone class follows trajectory exactly; anything else noise. also lets people vary around class trajectory: start rate change (random intercepts slopes). difference matters. people vary within kind, first model can express variation adding classes, tends find classes (Bauer Curran 2003). second model separates kinds change individual variation. one call. Persons classified units, id names class_level = "group" keeps person’s measurements one class; random adds random effects.

Ordinary latent profile analysis represents heterogeneity among observations finite mixture distributions. component, latent profile, characterized set indicator means variances. two-level formulation implemented multilpa() extends representation introducing latent classes group level. Observation-level profiles describe patterns indicators; group-level classes describe differences probabilities profiles. allows analysis distinguish variation among observations variation profile composition across groups. example, repeated measurements student engagement, observation-level profile may represent pattern relatively high activity across several indicators. student-level class may represent students whose observations frequently belong profile. Membership student class require every observation student engagement profile. distinction useful whenever within-person variation part research question. latents package provides estimation, result extraction, visualization, diagnostic procedures two-level mixture. extensions include categorical mixed indicators, membership covariates, missing-indicator likelihoods, staged estimation, latent transition analysis. tutorial develops continuous two-level model first, examines extensions relation analytical purposes.

title: Compare mixture regressions with different numbers of classes — enumerate_regressions
text: Fits mixture_regression() every requested number classes (crossed numbers group classes, two-level model) returns fit statistics one table. what: Reading growth of students nested in schools — growth_schools
title: Reading growth of students nested in schools — growth_schools
text: simulated multilevel longitudinal dataset multilevel growth mixture model. row one student's reading score one occasion: 600 students 40 schools (15 per school), tested five occasions (wave 0 4). Two kinds student follow two trajectories: improving (starts near 48, gains 3 points wave) plateauing (starts near 56, gains 0.3). Students vary around trajectory (random intercept SD 3, random slope SD 0.6, correlation -0.2; residual SD 2). Schools two types: supportive schools 80% students improve, struggling schools 25% , school's support programme (standardized, measured ) makes likely supportive. 8% tests missed random.

what: Achievement growth of students with three kinds of trajectory — growth_scores
title: Achievement growth of students with three kinds of trajectory — growth_scores
text: simulated longitudinal dataset growth models. row one student's test score one occasion: 300 students tested seven occasions (wave 0 6). Three kinds student follow three trajectories: improving (starts near 48, gains 3.5 points wave), stable (starts near 62, gains 0.5) declining (starts near 58, loses 2.5). Within kind, students vary around trajectory: start rate change (random intercept SD 4, random slope SD 0.8, correlation -0.3, spread every kind), residual SD 3. Motivation, measured , makes student likely improving less likely declining. 12% tests missed random, panel unbalanced.

what: Fit a finite mixture of regressions — mixture_regression
title: Fit a finite mixture of regressions — mixture_regression
text: Fits regression whose coefficients differ across n_classes latent classes returns fitted model: class-specific regressions, class sizes every row's posterior class membership, estimated jointly maximum likelihood. clusterwise, latent class mixture regression (DeSarbo Cron 1988; Wedel DeSarbo 1995).

title: Fit a finite mixture of regressions — mixture_regression
code: mixture_regression(   formula,   data,   n_classes,   family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial", "ordinal"),   id = NULL,   class_level = c("observation", "group"),   n_group_classes = 1L,   common = NULL,   membership = ~1,   group_membership = ~1,   variance = c("varying", "equal"),   n_starts = 10L,   max_iter = 1000L,   tol = 1e-08,   min_variance = 1e-06,   seed = NULL,   missing = c("error", "omit"),   select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),   vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg", "none"),   weights = NULL,   random = NULL,   random_covariance = c("varying", "equal", "proportional"),   random_diagonal = FALSE,   cluster = NULL,   residual_correlation = c("none", "ar", "brownian"),   residual_time = NULL )

title: Fit a finite mixture of regressions — mixture_regression
text: formula model formula outcome ~ predictors. Factors, interactions offset() supported. data data frame. n_classes Number regression classes. family "gaussian" (default), "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial" "ordinal" (proportional-odds cumulative logit; see Families). id NULL (default), name column identifying groups (persons, schools, ...). class_level "observation" (default; row class) "group" (rows group share class; requires id). n_group_classes Number second-level group classes (default 1, second level), class_level = "observation" id, clusters multilevel growth mixture (cluster). common NULL, predictor terms whose coefficients shared every class: variable names "age", one-sided formula ~ age. term must appear formula. membership Covariates predicting class membership (multinomial logit, first class reference): variable names "age", one-sided formula (~ 1, default, none). Row-level "observation"; constant within groups "group". group_membership Group-level covariates predicting group class, two-level model, names one-sided formula. Must constant within groups. variance "varying" (default; residual standard deviation, negative-binomial dispersion, per class) "equal" (one shared). Gaussian negative-binomial families . n_starts Number random starts (default 10), besides one start built residuals pooled regression. Every start runs 50 EM iterations; better half (least two) continue convergence. max_iter Maximum EM iterations per start (default 1000). tol Relative convergence tolerance log likelihood (default 1e-8). min_variance Floor Gaussian residual variance, relative outcome's variance (default 1e-6). Starts class reaches floor (fits rows exactly) set aside. seed NULL (default) integer seed. caller's random state restored afterwards. missing "error" (default) refuses rows missing values variable model uses; "omit" drops latents_rows_dropped warning stating many. select_start "likelihood" (default) keeps start highest likelihood; "converged" prefers best start converged. vcov_type Covariance estimates stored fit: "observed" (default; inverse observed information), "robust" (sandwich CR1 factor G / (G - 1), clustered top-level unit, id single-level fit given id) "opg" (outer product scores). "none" skips inference. weights NULL, name numeric column data sampling weight per independent unit: per row without id, per id group otherwise (constant within ). Pseudo maximum likelihood weights scaled sum number units; vcov_type defaults "robust" refuses "observed" "opg". information criteria use weighted log likelihood; entropy term ICL sums units' posteriors unweighted, profile models. random NULL (default; random effects), random effects within classes: variable names "time" (random intercept random slope time) "intercept" (random intercepts ), one-sided formula ~ 1 + time. slope without random intercept needs formula ~ 0 + time. See Growth mixture models. random_covariance random-effect covariance differs across classes: "varying" (default; one per class), "equal" (one shared matrix, lcmm::hlme() nwg = FALSE) "proportional" (shared matrix times class-specific scale, last class's one; nwg = TRUE). random_diagonal TRUE uncorrelated random effects (diagonal covariance, idiag = TRUE lcmm); default FALSE. cluster NULL (default), name column grouping persons (id) clusters, schools, multilevel growth mixture model (random): cluster belongs one n_group_classes group classes, sets trajectory-class probabilities persons. clusters independent units likelihood, standard errors BIC; n_group_classes = 1 model single-level growth mixture clusters units, comparable BIC fits group classes. See Growth mixture models. residual_correlation "none" (default) independent residuals within person; random, "ar" adds continuous-time autoregressive process, covariance sd^2 exp(-rate |t - s|), "brownian" Brownian motion, sd^2 min(t, s), residual variance, shared classes: lcmm::hlme(cor = AR(time)) cor = BM(time). model without process fitted first every start; process estimated jointly parameters. process data separate residual variance random effects left bound warned (latents_random_boundary); rows standard error. Refused latents_bad_argument without random. residual_time numeric column process runs ; default first numeric variable random, else predictors. Brownian motion needs non-negative times (latents_bad_data).

text: class_level n_group_classes choose one three likelihoods. Single level (id = NULL) Every row unit class. class_level = "group" rows group (id) belong class: regression mixture repeated measures, flexmix(y ~ x | id). group's likelihood contribution product rows' densities. class_level = "observation" id n_group_classes >= 2 row class, second-level group class sets class probabilities within groups (Vermunt 2003). n_group_classes = 1, id enters "robust" standard errors, clustered id.

title: Fit a finite mixture of regressions — mixture_regression
text: repeated measures persons (id, class_level = "group"), time predictor formula gives every class trajectory: latent class growth analysis (Nagin 2005). random adds random effects within classes, persons vary around class trajectory: growth mixture model (Verbeke Lesaffre 1996; Muthen Shedden 1999). Within class k, person 's outcomes $$y_i = X_i \beta_k + Z_i b_i + e_i, \quad b_i \sim N(0, G_k), \quad e_i \sim N(0, \sigma_k^2 ),$$ Z built random. likelihood exact (Gaussian, numerical integration); estimation EM random effects missing data, finished quasi-Newton analytic scores. fit class latents_growth_mixture; tables plots described get_results() plot(). Random effects require gaussian family, id class_level = "group". residual_correlation, residuals also carry process shared classes, \(e_i \sim N(0, W_i + \sigma_k^2 )\): continuous-time autoregressive process ("ar") Brownian motion ("brownian") residual_time, lcmm::hlme(cor = ); hlme's estimates two likelihoods agree (equivalence/test-growth-correlated-lcmm.R source repository). cluster, persons nested clusters (students schools) multilevel growth mixture model fitted: cluster belongs group class h, trajectory-class logits persons group-class-specific intercept shared covariate slopes, $$L = \prod_j \sum_h \omega_h \prod_{\j} \sum_k \pi_{k|h} f_k(y_i)$$ (Asparouhov Muthen 2008; Vermunt 2003). group_membership names cluster-level covariates group class. group classes returned get_results(fit, "group_classes") "clusters".

title: Fit a finite mixture of regressions — mixture_regression
text: "gaussian" (identity link, residual standard deviation per class, one shared variance = "equal"), "binomial" (logit link; outcome 0/1, logical, two-level factor whose second level success, cbind(successes, failures)), "poisson" (log link; offset() terms formula honoured) "negative_binomial" (log link, NB2: variance mu + alpha mu^2 dispersion alpha per class, one shared variance = "equal", overdispersed counts; dispersion estimated zero Poisson limit raises latents_boundary). "ordinal" fits cumulative-logit (proportional-odds) regression within class (McCullagh 1980), $$P(Y \le c \mid x, k) = F(t_{kc} - x'\beta_k), \quad c = 1, \ldots, C - 1,$$ ordered thresholds \(t_{k1} < \ldots < t_{k,C-1}\) per class place intercept, parametrization MASS::polr(): positive slope moves class towards higher categories. outcome ordered factor, factor (levels taken order) whole-number categories; categories observed, least two. common terms share slopes across classes, offset() honoured; formula's intercept replaced thresholds, must removed. thresholds appear coefficient table terms "threshold:<lower>|<upper>", exp_estimate slope cumulative odds ratio higher category. class "mean" ordinal outcome (fitted values, predict(), trajectories) expected category score \(\sum_c c P(Y = c)\), categories scored 1 C order; predict(type = "probabilities") gives category probabilities. one outcome per class assignment, ordinal mixture predictors two categories (logistic mixture "binomial") identified refused latents_not_identified, unless class_level = "group" gives class assignment several outcomes. single-level mixture also refused free parameters P (C - 1), number free category probabilities P distinct covariate patterns (example two classes one binary factor). mixture Bernoulli regressions one trial per unit identified (mixture Bernoullis Bernoulli), binary outcome requires class_level = "group" (several rows per class assignment) binomial counts one trial per row; binary specifications refused.
